what_it_does: This chip measures the electrical properties of biological tissues up to 30 megahertz—ten times faster than prior work—to diagnose conditions like dehydration, cancer, or soil water content. Traditional chips used I-Q demodulation (mixing a signal with two reference waves 90 degrees apart, like in old radio receivers) but suffered from phase errors larger than half a degree. This new chip replaces that analog mixing with time-to-digital demodulation: instead of multiplying signals, it measures the precise time difference between events, then reconstructs the phase information digitally. This eliminates the distortion that comes from analog multiplication and achieves sub-degree phase accuracy.
